title: First Agreement with China Covers Medical and Scientific Cooperation and a Smart Hospital in Mexico, Sheinbaum Says
author: Néstor Jiménez and Alma E. Muñoz
content:
_This article by[Néstor Jiménez and Alma E.
Muñoz](https://www.jornada.com.mx/autores/N%C3%A9stor%20Jim%C3%A9nez)
originally appeared in the [November 24, 2026 edition of La
Jornada](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/11/24/politica/primer-
acuerdo-con-china-cooperacion-medica-cientifica-y-el-primer-hospital-
inteligente-en-mexico-sheinbaum), Mexico's premier left wing daily newspaper._

**Mexico City.** President Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo explained that an initial
cooperation agreement had been reached with the [Chinese
government](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/11/23/economia/mexico-y-
china-acuerdan-mesa-de-trabajo-que-incluye-aumentar-exportaciones-al-pais-
asiatico) for medical training and scientific research, as well as to
establish the country’s **first smart hospital based on the Chinese model**.
However, there are more areas in which ties with the Asian giant are to be
expanded, including technological development, energy, the environment and
tourism.

At the same time, she stressed that another goal is to improve the trade
balance through increased exports to China.

Following her visit to Shenzhen, China, to attend the annual Asia-Pacific
Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit, the president said the specific objectives
include exchanges for scientific research and medical training, with the
intention that Mexicans can travel to the Asian country for that purpose and
vice versa.

> “We agreed on at least two actions for collaboration, for cooperation. The
> first is to establish a smart hospital in Mexico, to start with that and,
> from there, see how we can move forward in other hospitals. We still have
> not decided which hospital, but the hospital we visited has **1,500 beds**
> and has advanced technology and extraordinary care. The objective is to
> establish one of these hospitals in Mexico and continue collaborating from
> there. And the second is greater cooperation in training and scientific
> research, so that a group of Mexican doctors can go to China to train, to
> study, and also to see whether doctors from China can come to Mexico to
> train,” Sheinbaum Pardo said.

During her morning press conference this Tuesday, the president detailed the
areas in which cooperation with that country is being proposed.

> “The objective is to continue collaborating through China’s embassy in
> Mexico in health, science and technological development, energy, the
> environment and tourism. These are the five main areas in which we decided
> to advance cooperation further.”
>
> President Claudia Sheinbaum

She noted that Secretary of Environment and Natural Resources (Semarnat)
Alicia Bárcena; Energy Secretary Luz Elena González; and Economy Secretary
Marcelo Ebrard also attended to expand the dialogue.

The energy secretary stayed in that country to “analyze some technologies,
such as, for example, processing solid waste to generate energy, among others,
and also water treatment.”

Regarding tourism, she recalled that next year marks **55 years of Mexico-
China relations** , so it is proposed that it could be a special year for
tourism between the two nations. She also explained that it was in that
context that she asked the Chinese government to consider giving Mexico a
panda. She recalled that two pandas were given to the country in the 1970s,
and after they had offspring, it became “panda mania” among Mexicans.

On trade with China, she explained that the economy secretary also stayed in
that country after the APEC summit, and stressed that “part of what is on the
table is for us to export more products to China and achieve a better balance
in our trade.”
